title_pattern.notes: Rules-horror series title. 'New Household Rules' names the format (a list of rules for a house) but gives no stakes, no number and no creature; '(Pt2?)' with a question mark reads as uncertain/unplanned and tells cold viewers they missed part 1. Over half the title is generic hashtags (#viral #tiktok #trending), i.e. a TikTok repost habit. As a control it shows the baseline: format label + part number, no curiosity gap in the title itself.

thumbnail.composition: No custom thumbnail. yt-dlp maxres is an auto-picked frame at ~30.5 s: the girl in a red sweater, medium shot, front-on, hand on cheek, sleepy/sulky expression against a mint-green wall with a brown door frame, pillarboxed inside a blurred 16:9 copy. In the Shorts feed the effective thumbnail is frame 0: black 9:16 canvas, a 16:9 picture band across the middle third showing the back of the girl's head (red headband) in the left foreground staring at a dark wooden door at floor level, a glitch streak across the top, caption 'PEEK UNDER THE DOOR' below.
thumbnail.text: Only the burned-in caption: thin, scratchy, hand-lettered all-caps in white, centred just under the picture band ('IF YOU'RE TIRED AT NIGHT' on the auto thumb, 'PEEK UNDER THE DOOR' on frame 0). Small: roughly 6-7% of frame width per word.
thumbnail.colours: Black letterbox dominates (~65% of the frame). Inside the band: muted mint/sage greens, warm browns of doors and floor, one saturated red accent (headband + sweater) that becomes the character's colour signature across every shot.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Weak. Frame 0 subject faces away and the door is the 'subject' at floor level; the auto thumb is a calm medium shot. The only scale contrast in the video comes later (tiny girl in a wide doorway at 33 s vs. ECU face at 42 s).
thumbnail.why_it_works: As a control it mostly does not: the letterboxed band wastes two thirds of the feed tile, there is no face or threat on frame 0 and the caption is small. What it does right: the imperative caption ('PEEK UNDER THE DOOR') immediately signals the rules format, and the red-on-green character palette is consistent and recognisable for returning series viewers.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: Peek under the door to see if the lights in the living room are flickering. If they are,
hook.device: Cold open mid-list with a second-person imperative rule plus a conditional ('if they are... if not...'): the viewer is put in the house and given a task, no premise or setup. A 0.7 s full-screen kinetic card at 2.0 s repeats 'ARE FLICKERING' in 5 stacked rows with RGB glitch bands, acting out the word. Frame 0 also carries a glitch streak. Weakness for cold viewers: as 'Pt2' it never says whose rules these are or why, and the first rule references an unseen living room and an earlier bathroom check ('check the bathroom AGAIN').
hook.visual_0_5s: 0-2.0 s back-of-head OTS of the girl staring at a dark door at floor level (glitch line at 0 s); 2.0-2.8 s full-frame stacked 'ARE FLICKERING' text with green/blue/red glitch bands; 2.8-5 s back to the door shot with slow push-in, caption 'IF THEY ARE', then a red glitch flash.

beats.summary: Rule 1 as a second-person task: peek under the door, check whether the living-room lights flicker. Kinetic 'ARE FLICKERING' card at 2 s.
'If they are, stay put' (red glitch caption) / 'if not, check the bathroom again' - binary choice; 'again' implies events from part 1.
'Remember, don't open the door right away' - full-screen red stacked 'REMEMBER' card then a text-only black card: the rule is delivered as a warning with no picture.

'If the shadow disappears, bring in the blue and white things ASAP' - girl peering into a bathroom with teal puddles; the 'blue and white things' are never explained (colour-coded caption words make them feel important).
'Only turn off the light in the bathroom, keep all the other room lights on' - hand on light switch; yellow comic 'LIGHTS ON' punch text.
Fridge food: warm it up before eating, but don't eat it all up - mundane chore that implies someone or something else in the house needs the food.
'If you're tired at night, go to our room... you'll see a white closet. It's safe, don't worry' - the parents' room is presented as the safe zone; reassurance primes the scare.
'Before you go to bed, check on the closet carefully. Peek through the gap' - the safe object becomes the threat; profile CU at the closet gap, then ECU frightened face.

'If you see a blue eye staring from inside, shine your flashlight till it vanish' - face cuts to a colour-inverted magenta/blue glitch negative (jump-scare stand-in), then dissolves with chromatic blur = 'vanish'.
'One last thing before bed' (black card, red keywords): hang a bag on the outside door knob, lock the door, go rest - offering ritual with no explanation.
'Next morning you'll find the second note' - girl asleep, then sitting up holding a paper note; chains to the next part.

pacing.caption_style: 1 short phrase (2-6 words) at a time, all caps, swapped every ~1.5 s, timed to the voice
pacing.rehook_interval_s: ~5-6 s: each new rule is a mini re-hook; pattern interrupts (text cards / glitch / colour punch) at 2, 5, 9, 10, 22.5, 46.4, 50, 55 s
pacing.notes: Slow-ish narration (155 wpm, pauses of ~0.5-1 s between clauses) carried by visual interrupts rather than speech speed. Long holds on single images (door 0-9 s with interruptions, fridge 6.4 s) are the weakest stretches. Scare peak at 77-83% of runtime; cliffhanger in the last 2.5 s.

techniques_worth_copying: Rules-list format in second-person imperative with conditional branches ('if X, do Y; if not, do Z'): every rule is a self-contained micro-mystery and a natural re-hook every ~5 s.

Unexplained concrete specifics ('the blue and white things', 'hang a bag on the outside door knob', 'don't eat it all up') - the viewer infers an unseen presence; nothing is explained, which drives comments.

Colour-coded keyword captions tied to story objects (blue = shadow/eye, white = closet/things, red = warnings and the cliffhanger, yellow = light/flashlight). Cheap to do in code and makes key nouns pop.
Full-screen kinetic word-stack cards ('ARE FLICKERING' x5, 'REMEMBER' x8) with RGB glitch as 0.7-0.8 s pattern interrupts that act out the word.
Text-only black cards for the most important warnings and the transition into the final rule - silence of the picture = emphasis.
False-safety beat ('It's safe, don't worry') immediately before the safe object becomes the threat.
Jump-scare without a monster: colour-invert the protagonist's ECU face into a magenta/cyan negative with jitter, then chromatic-blur dissolve for 'vanish'. Fully reproducible with CSS/SVG filters.
Series cliffhanger ('next morning you'll find the second note') - a physical object that promises the next episode.
One recurring character with a fixed colour signature (red headband + red sweater) across every shot for series recognition.

AVOID (control lessons): letterboxed 16:9 band wasting ~65% of the 9:16 frame; starting a Pt2 with no premise for cold viewers; frame 0 with no face/threat; hashtag-stuffed title; 6-9 s holds on one static picture.

code_only_remake_requirements.layout: 1080x1920 black canvas. Picture band 1080x608 (16:9) centred at y~650-1258 (34-66%); caption line centred at y~1330 (~69%). Better for us: fill the full 9:16 frame and keep the caption at ~70%, since the letterbox is a weakness.
code_only_remake_requirements.typography: Thin, scratchy hand-lettered all-caps font (Google Fonts candidates: 'Rock Salt', 'Gochi Hand', 'Covered By Your Grace', 'Nanum Pen Script'); per-word colour tokens (white default, red #c8102e-ish warnings, blue #3a6fd8-ish, yellow #e8d33a, 'white' as white fill + black outline); a drippy red display font for the REMEMBER card (e.g. 'Creepster'); yellow outlined comic font for punch overlays (e.g. 'Bangers').
code_only_remake_requirements.scenes: ~11 flat/soft-shaded SVG interior illustrations: door + floorboards (low angle), tiled bathroom with cabinets/bin/puddles, wall light switch, open fridge shelves, mint-wall bedroom, wide bedroom doorway + white wardrobe, wardrobe-gap profile, bed + nightstand, door knob with plastic bag. Each needs a slow Ken Burns transform (scale 1.00->1.06-1.08 over the shot, optional x-drift).
code_only_remake_requirements.character: One SVG girl rig (black bob hair, red headband, red sweater) in 6 views: back-of-head OTS, back reaching up, front medium (hand-on-cheek pose), small full-body in doorway (2 poses: hands at sides, arms crossed), close profile, front ECU face with eye states (normal, wide/frightened, closed/asleep) and a sitting-up-with-note pose. Blink + subtle breathing loop to avoid dead stills.
code_only_remake_requirements.effects: RGB-split glitch (offset R/G/B layers + random horizontal slice displacement, coloured bars) for 0.3-1 s; colour inversion + hue-rotate + glow (CSS filter: invert(1) hue-rotate(...) saturate(3) + drop-shadow) for the scare; chromatic blur dissolve; white flash; zoom-blur transition (scale + motion blur); crossfade/ghost-double dissolve; full-screen stacked-text card component (N rows of the same word, vertical scroll ~1 row/0.2 s, per-row jitter, optional glitch bands behind); black text card; comic pop-in overlay text (scale 1.3->1 with outline).
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Local TTS narrator (Kokoro/Piper) at ~150-160 wpm with 0.5-1 s pauses between clauses; word timestamps from TTS or faster-whisper to drive caption swaps; continuous low drone/ambient bed (no gaps); SFX on every glitch/text card (static burst, sub hit), a sting on the inverted-face scare.
code_only_remake_requirements.data_model: storyboard: list of rules {line, condition_branch?, keywords:[{word,colour}], scene_id, character_pose, effect:(none|glitch|stack_card|black_card|invert_scare|punch_text), duration_from_tts}. Caption chunker splits each line into 2-6 word cards.
code_only_remake_requirements.effort_estimate: Moderate: the effects and caption system are simple; the cost is the 11 illustrated SVG scenes and the multi-view character rig. Reusable across a whole 'rules' series.
